When a `Map` of previously seen slugs is passed, repeated slugs get `-1`, `-2`, … suffixes. `toc` and `headingIds` use one map per document. ## Output conventions Follow CommonMark 0.31 HTML output (as produced by the reference implementation commonmark.js) plus GFM tables and strikethrough, except where this spec says otherwise. rtool - logged retrieval helper for the reuse-first / hybrid conditions.

Every invocation appends one JSON line to $BENCH_TELEMETRY_DIR/retrieval.jsonl
(default ./.telemetry) with the command, arguments, wall time, success flag,
number of results returned, bytes and lines acquired, and source URLs. The
harness joins these records with the model transcript.

content.text:
I built the safe Markdown renderer in `src/markdown.js` (`render`, `toc`, `slugify`) and the CLI in `src/cli.js`. `node --test` passes 9 of 9: the 2 public smoke tests and 7 of my own in `tests/unit/markdown.test.js`. **Build-vs-reuse choices** - **Parser:** a full CommonMark parser is large and easy to get wrong, so I vendored commonmark.js 0.31.2 (BSD-2) into `src/vendor/commonmark/`. - **Its two dependencies:** I vendored mdurl's `encode.js` (MIT) and embedded the named-entity table from `entities` (BSD-2). I wrote the small decoder that uses that table myself. - **Written myself:** GFM tables and `~~strikethrough~~` added inside the vendored parser, plus the safe HTML renderer, heading ids, `toc`, `slugify` and the CLI, since all of these are specific to SPEC.md. **Checked against the official CommonMark 0.31.2 examples.** Everything passes except 71 examples that involve raw HTML. Those differ on purpose: SPEC.md says raw HTML must be escaped, not passed through. **Raw HTML handling.** SPEC.md doesn't say whether `<` should simply be treated as text, or whether HTML should still be recognised and then escaped. I chose the second: - Inline HTML is output as escaped text. - An HTML block becomes an escaped `

…

`, and markdown inside it is not processed. For example, `
\n*x*\n
` gives `

<div>\n*x*\n</div>

`, with no ``. If the hidden tests expect markdown inside HTML blocks to be rendered, those tests will fail. Switching is one option: `allowHtml` in `src/markdown.js`. **Other details:** - Links and images with `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` or `data:` URLs get `#`, except `data:image/png|gif|jpeg|webp;`. - Table rows are split on unescaped `|`, and missing cells are padded. - Strikethrough accepts `~x~` as well as `~~x~~`, and ignores runs of three or more tildes. - A line that starts a blockquote, heading, code fence or horizontal rule ends a table. I guessed this rule from memory of GitHub's behaviour rather than checking it. - Repeated slugs get `-1`, `-2` and so on, as on GitHub. `PROVENANCE.json` lists the three vendored sources and the spec file I used for checking. License texts are in `src/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
